dog.description_text: Dani - 1 year & 35lbs, Collie/Aussie Mix, Spayed Want to see vidoes of her? Please click here. Our Team Says: This dog needs a home in the burbs - yard and calm area is her vibe. She can not do city life. Great with other dogs - currently in a foster home with a yard and two dogs and she's living her best life! This puppy is eligible to join our foster-to-adopt program. Please email fostertoadopt@socialteesnyc.org with the animal’s name in the subject line if you are interested! Want to straight up adopt? Submit an adoption application a t socialteesnyc.org Her Foster Mom Says : "Dani has been an absolute joy to take care of while she waits for her forever family. She exhibits all of the characteristics of a herding breed. She's sweet, highly intelligent, clever and independent. Although she is very high energy, she loves her breaks and naps like a typical puppy. She has an internal clock that wakes her up at the same time every day (I love that for me) and she knows when it's time for breakfast, snacks and dinner. If you're late for any of those, she will let you know with mouthy play ;) She does so well with my younger dog who is also a herding breed and she gives space to my senior dog who isn't as up to playtime (but that doesn't mean she doesn't try to rile her up from time to time). Dani loves to be outside and the sound of the leash and keys ignites so much excitement from her! Her walks get better by the day as she came terrified of loud sounds but is learning to adapt. She still gets spooked and might want to hightail it back to the house, but with a few calming pep talks and some treat motivation, she gets right back on track. She also loves to play wrestle and chase outside and tends to dig for treasures aka sticks! Her own designated dig box would be ideal!" Level of dog ownership experience required: INTERMEDIATE – As an adult, this dog will need significant structure and plenty of daily exercise, training, and mental stimulation – 90 consecutive minutes of movement in the morning plus potty break walks and brain games throughout the day. The adopter must have relevant primary care experience with a similar breed, temperament, and/or energy level. (Primary care experience includes ownership, fostering, or dog sitting as an adult, not a dog you grew up with.) Relevant puppy care experience is a huge plus, but bare minimum the adopter must have TONS of time and patience. Raising a puppy can be a lot of fun, but it’s also tremendous work. Puppies’ personalities and exercise/stimulation requirements change dramatically between now and when they’re a year old as their bodies and brains develop, so an active lifestyle and the ability to adapt to a pup’s evolving needs are a must. We strongly urge professional dog training with a rewards based trainer from the get go. Adults only or kids ages 8 and up – all puppies go through a mouthy, rambunctious phase and often accidentally hurt children when playing. PLEASE DO YOUR OWN BREED RESEARCH to make sure you have a better understanding of the kind of temperament and exercise requirements this dog may have as an adult. Energy level: MEDIUM – Needs a daily 60-90 minute walk or window of quick paced exercise (minimum) in addition to potty break strolls (10-30 min each). Also needs significant socializing opportunities outside the home and mental stimulation at home like tricks training practice, chew items, and puzzle toys. (This is regardless of dog size – many small breeds were designed for lots of activity and will exhibit unwanted behavior when they’re understimulated.) POTTY TRAINING - Yes she's potty trained. She's fully potty trained. TOLERANCE TO CITY - Can't do the city. Needs a home in the burbs :) COMFORT LEVEL WITH STRANGERS - She's shy at first with strangers but warms up to them quick. I have not witnessed any aggression or fear. BEHAVIOR WITH CHILDREN - Okay in a home with older kids. Too playful to be in a home with younger kids. SOCIAL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER DOGS - She is playful and social with dogs in the home/yard setting. When she sees dogs, she wants to play with them. She doesn't seem phased by the size of the dog. RESPECTFUL BEHAVIOR WITH OTHER ANIMALS - She chases and barks at squirrels. She hasn't had close up interaction/play with cats but she barks at them when she sees them in the neighbor's yard. MOUTHY BEHAVIOR - Very mouthy - wants to play with her mouth. Learning she can't do this with humans. But respectufl of belongings. SEPARATION ANXIETY - Will cry when you first leave her home alone. But then settles down. LEASH MANNERS - She is great with the leash. Only pulls if she gets spooked but for the most part, she's fine. CUDDLE BUG LEVEL - She is lower level! She comes to you and lays next to you but gets up for her own space pretty quickly. JUMPING ON PEOPLE TO SAY HELL O - She is definitely a jumper and needs more training. She listens to commands to get down unless she's really excited. CRATE TRAINING - She goes in and out whenever she wants. She lays in it for her alone time and to eat. If I need her to go in, she won't just go in it because she seems to know that means I have to leave lol. So I put a treat inside and she goes in. She does try to eat the food and treats of the other dogs, so I give her her food in the crate. Medical status: Healthy as far as we know. Up to date on their DHPP and Bordetella vaccines, spayed/neutered; microchipped; treated with dewormer upon intake. (For dogs under 4 months old, adopters will need to finish the DHPP vaccine series and administer the Rabies vaccine at 16 weeks of age.) How did this dog end up with Social Tees? Most of our dogs come via partner groups who help us save them from shelters where they are at risk of euthanasia in Tennessee, Los Angeles, and Puerto Rico. There are very few spay/neuter resources there and many more animals in those areas than there are people to adopt them. Rescue groups like ours bring them to the northeast where the desire for pets like these allows us to save their lives. PLEASE NOTE: We cannot guarantee any breed mix, exact age, or full grown size (if the dog is under a year old). We do our best with very educated guesses. This animal is not at the Social Tees office, all are in foster homes. LEARN MORE ABOUT US: socialteesnyc.org and Instagram @socialteesnyc
